title: Under I/O pressure the agent stalls for minutes on a user action, silently
description:
Mark 2026-11-27: "nothing ever should hang, lock up, or go silent when
sent something to process. ever. thats always a bug. nobody tolerates
lag in a chat service" and "unexplaned random or long lag in a chat
service is a killing antifeature".

## What was found

`private_queries_are_one_to_one_rooms` (crates/mimid-agent/tests/irc_v2.rs)
PASSES in 349.61 seconds. Cargo even prints "has been running for over
60 seconds".

It was not slow before today because it could not be: the wait it sits
in had a 15 second deadline, so the test FAILED instead. Removing that
deadline (bead mimid-67e0) did not break anything; it replaced a random
failure with a measurement, and the measurement is 5.8 minutes.

The test configures `sync_interval_ms = 100`, so the periodic sync is
not the delay. Something in creating or observing a one-to-one room
takes minutes, and nothing in the path says why.

## Why this is P0

This is not a test problem. A private query is a user opening a direct
message, and the path under this test is the one a person waits on.
Minutes of silence after sending something to process is the
antifeature, and the flaky 15s deadline was hiding it: a test that fails
one run in fifteen reads as a flaky test, so nobody looks for the cause.

## What to do

1. Find where the time goes. The wait helpers now print what they are
   waiting for, so a timed run of this test with `--nocapture` says
   which wait holds and for how long. That run is in progress.
2. Fix the lag, not the test.
3. Then check the other long runs for the same thing. `jmap_seed` at
   13s and `push` at 11s are suspicious for the same reason, and the
   whole suite's 2224 tests took around 20 minutes with deadlines
   hiding whatever else is slow.

## The lesson for the rest of the sweep

Every deadline removed in bead mimid-67e0 may uncover one of these. That
is the point rather than a cost: a guessed timeout converts a latency
bug into an intermittent failure, which is the form in which it gets
ignored.

## Timed run, 2026-11-27

The wait helpers' own output, timestamped. Test ran 00:18:57 to 00:25:23.

  00:18:57  test starts
  00:22:14  first "waiting for a line from the server"   <- 3m17s gap
  00:22:19  ten lines exchanged in five seconds
  00:24:23  the next line, at "seen 10"                  <- 2m04s gap
  00:24:28  16s gap, then 14s, then 18s
  00:25:19  "waiting for the daemon to stop"
  00:25:23  passes

## Why it finishes at all, rather than failing

`Irc::until` reads lines until one matches, and the IRC front end sends
PING after 90 seconds of silence (DEFAULT_PING_AFTER, lib.rs:145). So a
keepalive hands the reader a line, it does not match, and the wait goes
round again. The 2m04s gap is about two keepalive periods. That is why
removing the 15s deadline turned a failure into a slow pass instead of a
hang.

## What the gaps are around

The test registers alice and bob on the SAME provider, then alice sends
the first PRIVMSG to bob, which creates a one-to-one room. So the slow
step is opening a direct message with someone for the first time: MLS
group creation, the KeyPackage fetch and the Welcome, any of which could
be sitting on a retry.

A person opening a DM waits on exactly this path. Minutes is the
antifeature.

## Next

A debug-level run of the same test is in progress to name the step that
holds. Until it lands this bead says where the time is, not yet why.

## Correction, 2026-11-27: it is intermittent, not always

A third run of the same test finished in 11.77 seconds, with every wait
logged inside a four second window and no gap at all. So the earlier
claim here -- that this path takes minutes -- is wrong as stated. The
three runs were 349.61s, 375.65s and 11.77s.

What the slow runs had in common: both followed a `cargo clean`, so a
full rebuild ran first and the page cache was cold, and the filesystem
had just had 178 GiB freed.

That points at the same thing the original gate failure showed, which
was a SQLite `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` taking 2.414809295 seconds --
a statement that should be microseconds. Under I/O pressure the agent's
database work goes orders of magnitude slower, and this path does enough
of it to stall for minutes.

## So the bug, restated

Not "opening a DM takes minutes". It is: under I/O pressure the agent
stalls for minutes on a user action, with nothing logged to say what it
is waiting for. A person would see a chat client go silent after sending
the first message to someone, with no indication whether it failed.

Dropping P0 to P1. The lag is real and reproducible under load, but it
is not the unconditional six minutes this bead first claimed, and the
difference matters for anyone who picks it up.

## What is still worth doing

1. The agent logs nothing across a multi-minute stall. The test harness
   installs no tracing subscriber, so the in-process daemon's own
   logging goes nowhere, which is why this took three runs to
   characterise. Both halves are worth fixing: the daemon should say
   what it is waiting on, and the harness should capture it.
2. Find what the path does enough of to be that sensitive to I/O. A
   first DM creates a one-to-one room: MLS group creation, a KeyPackage
   fetch, a Welcome. If any step writes and fsyncs per message rather
   than per batch, that is the multiplier.
3. The 2.4s PRAGMA deserves its own look. WAL mode is set per
   connection; if the agent opens connections per operation rather than
   pooling, every one pays that.
notes: 2026-11-27: the three remaining actions are now beads mimid-604m.1 (no tracing subscriber in the harness, nothing logged across the stall), mimid-604m.2 (what the first-DM path does that makes it I/O-sensitive by 30x), mimid-604m.3 (the 2.4s PRAGMA and connection pooling). .2 is blocked on .1.
